-- A tokenizer and recursive-descent parser for arithmetic, with variables and errors.

local function tokenize(source)
	local tokens = {}
	local i = 1
	while i <= #source do
		local c = source:sub(i, i)
		if c:match("%s") then
			i += 1
		elseif c:match("%d") then
			local number = source:match("^%d+%.?%d*", i)
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = "number", value = tonumber(number) })
			i += #number
		elseif c:match("[%a_]") then
			local name = source:match("^[%a_][%w_]*", i)
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = "name", value = name })
			i += #name
		elseif c:match("[%+%-%*/%^%(%)=]") then
			table.insert(tokens, { kind = c })
			i += 1
		else
			error(`unexpected character '{c}' at {i}`, 0)
		end
	end
	table.insert(tokens, { kind = "end" })
	return tokens
end

local Parser = {}
Parser.__index = Parser

function Parser.new(tokens, variables)
	return setmetatable({ tokens = tokens, pos = 1, variables = variables }, Parser)
end

function Parser:peek()
	return self.tokens[self.pos].kind
end

function Parser:take(kind)
	local token = self.tokens[self.pos]
	if kind and token.kind ~= kind then
		error(`expected {kind}, got {token.kind}`, 0)
	end
	self.pos += 1
	return token
end

local PRECEDENCE = { ["+"] = 1, ["-"] = 1, ["*"] = 2, ["/"] = 2, ["^"] = 3 }

function Parser:primary()
	local token = self:take()
	if token.kind == "number" then
		return token.value
	elseif token.kind == "name" then
		local value = self.variables[token.value]
		if value == nil then
			error(`unknown variable {token.value}`, 0)
		end
		return value
	elseif token.kind == "-" then
		return -self:expression(3)
	elseif token.kind == "(" then
		local value = self:expression(0)
		self:take(")")
		return value
	end
	error(`unexpected {token.kind}`, 0)
end

function Parser:expression(minimum)
	local left = self:primary()
	while true do
		local op = self:peek()
		local precedence = PRECEDENCE[op]
		if not precedence or precedence <= minimum and op ~= "^" or precedence < minimum then
			return left
		end
		self:take()
		local right = self:expression(op == "^" and precedence - 1 or precedence)
		if op == "+" then
			left += right
		elseif op == "-" then
			left -= right
		elseif op == "*" then
			left *= right
		elseif op == "/" then
			if right == 0 then
				error("division by zero", 0)
			end
			left /= right
		else
			left ^= right
		end
	end
end

local function run(line, variables)
	local tokens = tokenize(line)
	local target
	if tokens[2].kind == "=" then
		target = tokens[1].value
		table.remove(tokens, 1)
		table.remove(tokens, 1)
	end
	local parser = Parser.new(tokens, variables)
	local value = parser:expression(0)
	parser:take("end")
	if target then
		variables[target] = value
	end
	return value
end

local variables = { pi = math.pi }
for _, line in { "x = 2 + 3 * 4", "y = (x - 4) ^ 2 / 2", "x * y - -3", "r = 2", "pi * r ^ 2", "1 / (x - 14)", "z + 1", "3 $ 4" } do
	local ok, result = pcall(run, line, variables)
	print(line, "=>", if ok then string.format("%.4g", result) else `error: {result}`)
end

	return function()
		value += step
		return value
	end, function()
		value = start
	end

	local cache = {}

		end
		return hit
	end

	if n < 2 then

	end

	end

-- 300 conditions with a dead `false and` part. A decompiler that retries a nested `if` on a

	table.insert(out, 0)
	if n + 1 > 1 then
		table.insert(out, 1)
		if n + 2 > 2 then
			table.insert(out, 2)
			if n + 3 > 3 then

					if n + 5 > 0 then

entries.source:
-- getfenv and setfenv: once a script touches environments, the compiler stops assuming globals
-- are what they look like, so builtins aren't folded, fast calls check the environment and
-- imports are looked up again. A decompiler has to keep every global a global
local function area(r)
	return math.floor(math.pi * r * r)
end
print(area(2))

local fake = {
	math = {
		pi = 3,
		floor = function(x)
			return "floor " .. x
		end,
	},
}
setfenv(area, setmetatable(fake, { __index = getfenv() }))
print(area(2))
print(getfenv(area) == fake, getfenv(1) == getfenv(print))

-- a global written through one environment is invisible from another
local function writer()
	shared_value = "written"
	return shared_value
end
setfenv(writer, setmetatable({}, { __index = getfenv() }))
print(writer(), rawget(getfenv(writer), "shared_value"), shared_value)

-- setfenv(1, ...) swaps the running function's own environment
local function sandboxed()
	setfenv(1, setmetatable({ tag = "inside" }, { __index = getfenv(2) }))
	return tag, type(print), type(math.floor)
end
print(sandboxed())
print(tag)

-- a function's environment is shared with the closures it makes
local function maker()
	return function()
		return label

-- evaluation order a decompiler can't move: locals used once whose calls have side effects,
-- the operands of > and >= (compiled as < and <= with the operands swapped), a method call's
-- object and arguments, and values read before a later write or call changes them
local trace = {}
local function note(tag, value)
	table.insert(trace, tag)
	return value
end
local function flush(label)
	print(label, table.concat(trace, " "))
	table.clear(trace)
end

-- two locals used once each, in the opposite order: inlining both would swap the calls
local first = note("a", 1)
local second = note("b", 2)
print(second, first)
flush("locals")

-- > and >= compile to LT and LE with the operands swapped, but they still run left to right
print(note("l", 3) > note("r", 2), note("l", 1) >= note("r", 1), note("l", "x") < note("r", "y"))
flush("compare")
print(not (note("l", 1) <= note("r", 2)), note("l", 2) ~= note("r", 2))
flush("compare not")
if note("cond l", 5) > note("cond r", 4) then
	note("then", nil)
end
flush("branch")

-- the object of a method call is worked out once, before its arguments
local obj = { n = 0 }
function obj:add(k)
	self.n += k
	return self
end
local function getobj()
	note("obj", nil)
	return obj
end
getobj():add(note("arg", 1)):add(note("arg2", 2))
print(obj.n)
flush("method")

-- a value read into a local before the table changes keeps the old value
local t = { v = "old" }
local saved = t.v
t.v = "new"
print(saved, t.v)
local box = { 1, 2, 3 }
local len = #box
table.insert(box, 4)
print(len, #box)

-- a call that changes a local the same argument list reads before and after it
local counter = 0
local function bump()
	counter += 1
	return counter
end
print(counter, bump(), counter + 0, bump())
local before = counter
bump()
print(before, counter)

-- an index read before a call in the same expression moves it
local arr = { 10, 20, 30 }
local i = 1
local function advance()
	i += 1
	return 0
end
print(arr[i] + advance(), arr[i])

-- every operand runs left to right before anything combines, right-associative or not
print(note("1", "a") .. note("2", "b") .. note("3", "c"))
flush("concat")
print(note("x", 2) ^ note("y", 3) ^ note("z", 1), note("p", 10) - note("q", 3) - note("r", 2))
flush("arith")

-- and / or only run what they need
local hit = note("left", false) and note("never", true) or note("right", "ok")
print(hit)
flush("logic")

-- a constructor evaluates its entries in order, keyed or not
local made = { note("one", 1), k = note("key", 2), note("two", 3), [note("ikey", "x")] = note("ival", 4) }
print(made[1], made[2], made.k, made.x)
flush("constructor")

-- an assignment reads its target table before the right-hand side runs, so a call that replaces
-- the table writes into the old one
local holder = { inner = { v = 0 } }
local function swap()
	note("swap", nil)
	local old = holder.inner
	holder.inner = { v = 100 }
	return old.v + 1
end
holder.inner.v = swap()
print(holder.inner.v)
flush("target")

-- Luau's experimental `if local` / `while local` / `const` syntax (a friend's case). The binding
-- lives only in the then-branch or loop body, so an outer variable with the same name has to
-- stay visible in the else-branch, and every loop iteration gets a fresh local for closures.
do
	const t = {1, 2, 3}
	while local v = table.remove(t) do
		print(v, #t)
	end
end
do
	local items = {"a", "b", false, "c"}
	local i = 0
	local function nextItem()
		i += 1
		return items[i]
	end
	-- false ends the loop just like nil
	while const item = nextItem() do
		print("item", item)
	end
	print("stopped at", i)
end
do
	local fns = {}
	local queue = {10, 20, 30}
	while local n = table.remove(queue, 1) do
		table.insert(fns, function()
			return n
		end)
	end
	print(fns[1](), fns[2](), fns[3]())
end
do
	local x = "outer"
	if local x = nil then
		print("then", x)
	else
		print("else", x)
	end
	if local x = "inner" then
		print("then", x)
	end
	print("after", x)
end
do
	local function classify(s)
		if local n: number? = tonumber(s) then
			return "number " .. n * 2
		elseif local first = string.match(s, "^%a+") then
			return "word " .. first
		elseif const sym = string.match(s, "^%p") then
			return "symbol " .. sym
		else
			return "other"
		end
	end
	print(classify("21"), classify("hello world"), classify("!?"), classify("  "))
end
do
	local function lookup(t, k)
		return if local v = t[k] then v .. "!" else "missing"
	end
	local map = {a = "x", b = "y"}
	print(lookup(map, "a"), lookup(map, "z"))
	const limit = 3
	local count = 0
	while local v = count < limit and count do
		count = v + 1
	end
	print("count", count)
end

--!strict

Inventory.__index = Inventory

local ITEMS = {
	sword = { weight = 8, stack = 1, value = 120 },
	potion = { weight = 1, stack = 10, value = 25 },
	arrow = { weight = 0.1, stack = 64, value = 1 },
	shield = { weight = 12, stack = 1, value = 90 },
}

function Inventory.new(capacity)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Inventory)
	self.capacity = capacity
	self.slots = {}
	self.weight = 0
	return self
end

local function round(n, places)
	local scale = 10 ^ places
	return math.floor(n * scale + 0.5) / scale
end

function Inventory:add(name, count)
	local info = ITEMS[name]
	if not info then
		return false, `unknown item {name}`
	end
	if self.weight + info.weight * count > self.capacity then
		return false, `too heavy: {round(self.weight + info.weight * count, 1)} > {self.capacity}`
	end
	local left = count
	for _, slot in self.slots do
		if slot.name == name and slot.count < info.stack then
			local moved = math.min(info.stack - slot.count, left)
			slot.count += moved
			left -= moved
			if left == 0 then
				break
			end
		end
	end
	while left > 0 do
		local moved = math.min(info.stack, left)
		table.insert(self.slots, { name = name, count = moved })
		left -= moved
	end
	self.weight += info.weight * count
	return true
end

function Inventory:remove(name, count)
	for i = #self.slots, 1, -1 do
		local slot = self.slots[i]
		if slot.name ~= name then
			continue
		end
		local taken = math.min(slot.count, count)
		slot.count -= taken
		count -= taken
		self.weight -= ITEMS[name].weight * taken
		if slot.count == 0 then
			table.remove(self.slots, i)
		end
		if count == 0 then
			return true
		end
	end
	return count == 0
end

function Inventory:report()
	local totals = {}
	for _, slot in self.slots do
		totals[slot.name] = (totals[slot.name] or 0) + slot.count
	end

	end
	table.sort(names, function(a, b)
		return ITEMS[a].value * totals[a] > ITEMS[b].value * totals[b]
	end)

-- closures made in loops: each iteration of a for loop has its own variable, a while loop's
-- local is fresh each time round, and an upvalue written after capture is shared
local fns = {}
for i = 1, 3 do
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		return i
	end
end
local k = 0
while k < 3 do
	k += 1
	local j = k * 10
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		return j
	end
end
for _, v in ipairs({ "a", "b" }) do
	local copy = v
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		copy = copy .. "!"
		return copy
	end
end
for idx, f in ipairs(fns) do
	print(idx, f(), f())
end

-- one variable captured by two closures, then changed from outside
local function counter()
	local n = 0
	local function inc()
		n += 1
		return n
	end
	local function get()
		return n
	end
	n = 100
	return inc, get
end
local inc, get = counter()
inc()
print(get(), inc(), get())

-- a loop variable shadowed inside the body, and the outer one read after
local total = 0
for i = 1, 4 do
	local i = i * 2
	total += i
end
local i = "outer"
print(total, i)

-- the loop body's local captured, then the loop exits early
local saved
for n = 1, 10 do
	local sq = n * n
	if sq > 20 then
		saved = function()
			return sq
		end
		break
	end
end
print(saved())

-- repeat whose condition reads a local from the body, captured by a closure there
local seen = {}
local r = 0
repeat
	r += 1
	local stop = r >= 3
	seen[r] = function()
		return stop
	end
until stop
print(r, seen[1](), seen[3]())

-- breaks, continues and returns out of loops, each checked by running both versions
do
	local function find(t, x)
		local found = nil
		for i, v in t do
			if v == x then
				found = i
				break
			end
		end
		if found == nil then
			return "none"
		end
		return found
	end
	print(find({1, 5, 3, 5}, 5), find({1, 2}, 9), find({}, 1))
end
do
	local function first_even(n)
		local r
		for i = 1, n do
			if i % 2 == 0 and i > 3 then
				r = i
				break
			end
		end
		return r
	end
	print(first_even(10), first_even(3))
end
do
	local function f(a, t)
		local hit = 0
		if a then
			for _, v in t do
				if v > 2 then
					hit = v
					break
				end
			end
		else
			hit = -1
		end
		return hit * 10
	end
	print(f(true, {1, 3, 4}), f(true, {1}), f(false, {9}))
end
do
	local out = {}
	for i = 1, 4 do
		for j = 1, 4 do
			if j > i then
				break
			end
			if (i + j) % 2 == 1 then
				continue
			end
			table.insert(out, i * 10 + j)
		end
		if i == 3 then
			continue
		end

-- metamethods: arithmetic, comparison, concat, call, index and newindex functions, len and unm,
-- and the raw functions that skip them
local Vec = {}
Vec.__index = Vec
local function vec(x, y)
	return setmetatable({ x = x, y = y }, Vec)
end
Vec.__add = function(a, b)
	return vec(a.x + b.x, a.y + b.y)
end
Vec.__sub = function(a, b)
	return vec(a.x - b.x, a.y - b.y)
end
Vec.__mul = function(a, b)
	if type(a) == "number" then
		return vec(a * b.x, a * b.y)
	end
	return vec(a.x * b, a.y * b)
end
Vec.__unm = function(a)
	return vec(-a.x, -a.y)
end
Vec.__eq = function(a, b)
	return a.x == b.x and a.y == b.y
end
Vec.__lt = function(a, b)
	return a.x * a.x + a.y * a.y < b.x * b.x + b.y * b.y
end
Vec.__le = function(a, b)
	return not (b < a)
end
Vec.__len = function(a)
	return math.sqrt(a.x * a.x + a.y * a.y)
end
Vec.__concat = function(a, b)
	local function s(v)
		return if type(v) == "table" then `({v.x}, {v.y})` else tostring(v)
	end
	return s(a) .. s(b)
end
Vec.__call = function(self, k)
	return self[k]
end
function Vec:dot(o)
	return self.x * o.x + self.y * o.y
end

-- true. Also and/or chains where a false or nil value in the middle changes which side wins
local nan = 0 / 0
local values = { 1, -1, 0, nan, math.huge, -math.huge }

local function compare(a, b)
	local out = {}
	if not (a < b) then out[#out + 1] = "!lt" end
	if not (a <= b) then out[#out + 1] = "!le" end
	if not (a > b) then out[#out + 1] = "!gt" end
	if not (a >= b) then out[#out + 1] = "!ge" end
	if a ~= a then out[#out + 1] = "self" end
	if not (a == b) then out[#out + 1] = "!eq" end
	while not (a < b) do
		out[#out + 1] = "w"
		break
	end
	local rounds = 0
	repeat
		rounds += 1
		out[#out + 1] = "r"
	until not (a > b) or rounds == 2
	return table.concat(out, ",")
end

	for j = 1, #values do
		print(i, j, compare(values[i], values[j]))
	end
end

	local x = a and b or c
	local y = a and (b or c)
	local z = (a or b) and c
	local w = not a == not b

	local u = a == nil and b or nil

-- metatable classes with methods
local Account = {}
Account.__index = Account

function Account.new(owner, balance)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Account)
	self.owner = owner
	self.balance = balance or 0
	self.history = {}
	return self
end

function Account:deposit(amount)
	if amount <= 0 then
		error("deposit must be positive")
	end
	self.balance += amount
	table.insert(self.history, { kind = "deposit", amount = amount })
end

function Account:withdraw(amount)
	if amount > self.balance then
		return false, "insufficient funds"
	end
	self.balance -= amount
	table.insert(self.history, { kind = "withdraw", amount = amount })
	return true
end

function Account:statement()
	local lines = {}
	for index, entry in ipairs(self.history) do
		lines[index] = ("%s %d"):format(entry.kind, entry.amount)
	end
	return table.concat(lines, "\n")
end

local savings = Account.new("sam", 100)
savings:deposit(50)
local ok, reason = savings:withdraw(500)
if not ok then
	print(reason)
end
print(savings:statement())

-- A* on a small grid map, with a binary heap for the open set.

local MAP = {
	"S....#....",
	".##..#.##.",
	".#...#..#.",
	".#.###..#.",
	"...#....#G",
	"##.#.####.",
	"..........",
}

local function parse(rows)
	local grid, start, goal = {}, nil, nil
	for y, row in ipairs(rows) do
		grid[y] = {}
		for x = 1, #row do
			local c = row:sub(x, x)
			grid[y][x] = c ~= "#"
			if c == "S" then
				start = { x = x, y = y }
			elseif c == "G" then
				goal = { x = x, y = y }
			end
		end
	end
	return grid, start, goal
end

local function key(x, y)
	return y * 1000 + x
end

local function heuristic(a, b)
	return math.abs(a.x - b.x) + math.abs(a.y - b.y)
end

local Heap = {}
Heap.__index = Heap

function Heap.new()
	return setmetatable({ items = {}, size = 0 }, Heap)
end

function Heap:push(node, priority)
	self.size += 1
	local i = self.size
	self.items[i] = { node = node, priority = priority }
	while i > 1 do
		local parent = i // 2
		if self.items[parent].priority <= self.items[i].priority then
			break
		end
		self.items[parent], self.items[i] = self.items[i], self.items[parent]
		i = parent
	end
end

function Heap:pop()
	if self.size == 0 then
		return nil
	end
	local top = self.items[1]
	self.items[1] = self.items[self.size]
	self.items[self.size] = nil
	self.size -= 1
	local i = 1
	while true do
		local smallest, left, right = i, i * 2, i * 2 + 1
		if left <= self.size and self.items[left].priority < self.items[smallest].priority then
			smallest = left
		end
		if right <= self.size and self.items[right].priority < self.items[smallest].priority then
			smallest = right
		end
		if smallest == i then
			break
		end
		self.items[smallest], self.items[i] = self.items[i], self.items[smallest]
		i = smallest
	end
	return top.node
end

local DIRECTIONS = { { 1, 0 }, { -1, 0 }, { 0, 1 }, { 0, -1 } }

local function findPath(grid, start, goal)
	local open = Heap.new()
	local cameFrom, cost = {}, { [key(start.x, start.y)] = 0 }
	open:push(start, heuristic(start, goal))
	local visited = 0
	while open.size > 0 do
		local current = open:pop()
		visited += 1
		if current.x == goal.x and current.y == goal.y then
			local path = { current }
			local k = key(current.x, current.y)
			while cameFrom[k] do
				current = cameFrom[k]
				table.insert(path, 1, current)
				k = key(current.x, current.y)
			end
			return path, visited
		end
		for _, d in DIRECTIONS do
			local nx, ny = current.x + d[1], current.y + d[2]
			if not (grid[ny] and grid[ny][nx]) then
				continue
			end
			local nk = key(nx, ny)
			local newCost = cost[key(current.x, current.y)] + 1
			if cost[nk] == nil or newCost < cost[nk] then
				cost[nk] = newCost
				cameFrom[nk] = current
				local next = { x = nx, y = ny }
				open:push(next, newCost + heuristic(next, goal))
			end
		end
	end
	return nil, visited
end

local grid, start, goal = parse(MAP)
local path, visited = findPath(grid, start, goal)
if path then
	local steps = {}
	for i, p in path do
		steps[i] = `({p.x},{p.y})`
	end
	print(`found a path of {#path - 1} steps after visiting {visited} cells`)
	print(table.concat(steps, " "))
else
	print("no path")
end

	end

		return "inside " .. kind
	end
	return "outside " .. kind

	if type(payload) == "table" then
		local kind = payload.kind
		if kind == A.Asset or kind == A.Bundle or kind == A.Look then
			return true
		end
	end
	if requestType == B.GamePass or requestType == B.Product then
		return true
	end
	return false
end
local function pick(state)
	if state == nil then
		return nil
	end
	if not isSupported(state.payload, state.request and state.request.kind) then
		return nil
	end
	return state.price
end

-- a loop whose end is the end of the function, through an if
local function scan(list, limit)
	if #list > 0 then
		local i = 0
		repeat
			i += 1
			if list[i] == limit then
				count += 100
				break
			end
		until i >= #list
	elseif limit then
		count += 1
	end

	local Z = folder.Z

		or (if Y then Y:IsA("FloatCurve") and #Y:GetKeys() > 0 else false)
		or (if Z then Z:IsA("FloatCurve") and #Z:GetKeys() > 0 else false)

	function obj.get()

	end
	return obj
end

	local copy = setmetatable({ x = self.x }, Class)
	return copy
end

	return function(n)

	return obj
end

	local handlers = {}
	return {

		end,
		Fire = function(_, ...)
			for _, f in handlers do
				f(...)
			end
		end,
	}
end

-- tables changed through metamethods and table.insert/remove, coroutines resumed for their side
-- effects, and what the chunk returns. Only what's left behind tells a right decompile from a

local function track(t, name)
	return setmetatable({}, {
		__index = t,
		__newindex = function(_, k, v)
			table.insert(log, name .. "." .. tostring(k))
			rawset(t, k, v)
		end,
	})
end

local config = track({}, "config")
config.speed = 16
config.jump = 50
config.speed += 4

for i = 1, 5 do
	if i % 2 == 0 then
		table.insert(registry, i * i)
	elseif i == 5 then
		registry.last = i
	end
end
table.remove(registry, 1)

function string.shout(s)
	return s:upper() .. "!"
end

counter = 0
local worker = coroutine.wrap(function()
	for _ = 1, 3 do
		counter += 1
		coroutine.yield()
	end
end)
worker()
worker()

temporary = true
temporary = nil

local swapped = { a = 1, b = 2 }
swapped.a, swapped.b = swapped.b, swapped.a
settings = { config = config, swapped = swapped, log = log }

print("done")
return #log, registry.last, ("hi"):shout()

-- closures made in loops: each iteration of a for loop has its own variable, a while loop's
-- local is fresh each time round, and an upvalue written after capture is shared

for i = 1, 3 do
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		return i
	end
end
local k = 0
while k < 3 do
	k += 1
	local j = k * 10
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		return j
	end
end
for _, v in ipairs({ "a", "b" }) do
	local copy = v
	fns[#fns + 1] = function()
		copy = copy .. "!"
		return copy
	end
end
for idx, f in ipairs(fns) do
	print(idx, f(), f())
end

	local n = 0
	local function inc()
		n += 1
		return n
	end
	local function get()
		return n
	end
	n = 100
	return inc, get
end

	total += i
end
end

	total += i
end

	r += 1
	local stop = r >= 3
	seen[r] = function()
		return stop
	end
until stop
print(r, seen[1](), seen[3]())

-- rosetta mutant mut1-17 of pathfinding: wrap for twice
-- A* on a small grid map, with a binary heap for the open set.

local MAP = {
	"S....#....",
	".##..#.##.",
	".#...#..#.",
	".#.###..#.",
	"...#....#G",
	"##.#.####.",
	"..........",
}

local function parse(rows)
	local grid, start, goal = {}, nil, nil
	for y, row in ipairs(rows) do
		grid[y] = {}
		for x = 1, #row do
			local c = row:sub(x, x)
			grid[y][x] = c ~= "#"
			if c == "S" then
				start = { x = x, y = y }
			elseif c == "G" then
				goal = { x = x, y = y }
			end
		end
	end
	return grid, start, goal
end

local function key(x, y)
for _ = 1, 2 do
	return y * 1000 + x
end
end

local function heuristic(a, b)
	return math.abs(a.x - b.x) + math.abs(a.y - b.y)
end

local Heap = {}
Heap.__index = Heap

function Heap.new()
	return setmetatable({ items = {}, size = 0 }, Heap)
end

function Heap:push(node, priority)
	self.size += 1
	local i = self.size
	self.items[i] = { node = node, priority = priority }
	while i > 1 do
		local parent = i // 2
		if self.items[parent].priority <= self.items[i].priority then
			break
		end
		self.items[parent], self.items[i] = self.items[i], self.items[parent]
		i = parent
	end
end

function Heap:pop()
	if self.size == 0 then
		return nil
	end
	local top = self.items[1]
	self.items[1] = self.items[self.size]
	self.items[self.size] = nil
	self.size -= 1
	local i = 1
	while true do
		local smallest, left, right = i, i * 2, i * 2 + 1
		if left <= self.size and self.items[left].priority < self.items[smallest].priority then
			smallest = left
		end
		if right <= self.size and self.items[right].priority < self.items[smallest].priority then
			smallest = right
		end
		if smallest == i then
			break
		end
		self.items[smallest], self.items[i] = self.items[i], self.items[smallest]
		i = smallest
	end
	return top.node
end

local DIRECTIONS = { { 1, 0 }, { -1, 0 }, { 0, 1 }, { 0, -1 } }

local function findPath(grid, start, goal)
	local open = Heap.new()
	local cameFrom, cost = {}, { [key(start.x, start.y)] = 0 }
	open:push(start, heuristic(start, goal))
	local visited = 0
	while open.size > 0 do
		local current = open:pop()
		visited += 1
		if current.x == goal.x and current.y == goal.y then
			local path = { current }
			local k = key(current.x, current.y)
			while cameFrom[k] do
				current = cameFrom[k]
				table.insert(path, 1, current)
				k = key(current.x, current.y)
			end
			return path, visited
		end
		for _, d in DIRECTIONS do
			local nx, ny = current.x + d[1], current.y + d[2]
			if not (grid[ny] and grid[ny][nx]) then
				continue
			end
			local nk = key(nx, ny)
			local newCost = cost[key(current.x, current.y)] + 1
			if cost[nk] == nil or newCost < cost[nk] then
				cost[nk] = newCost
				cameFrom[nk] = current
				local next = { x = nx, y = ny }
				open:push(next, newCost + heuristic(next, goal))
			end
		end
	end
	return nil, visited
end

local grid, start, goal = parse(MAP)
local path, visited = findPath(grid, start, goal)
if path then
	local steps = {}
	for i, p in path do
		steps[i] = `({p.x},{p.y})`
	end
	print(`found a path of {#path - 1} steps after visiting {visited} cells`)
	print(table.concat(steps, " "))
else
	print("no path")
end

-- evaluation order a decompiler can't move: locals used once whose calls have side effects,
-- the operands of > and >= (compiled as < and <= with the operands swapped), a method call's
-- object and arguments, and values read before a later write or call changes them

local function note(tag, value)
	table.insert(trace, tag)
	return value
end
local function flush(label)
	print(label, table.concat(trace, " "))
	table.clear(trace)
end

-- two locals used once each, in the opposite order: inlining both would swap the calls
local first = note("a", 1)
local second = note("b", 2)
print(second, first)
flush("locals")

-- > and >= compile to LT and LE with the operands swapped, but they still run left to right
print(note("l", 3) > note("r", 2), note("l", 1) >= note("r", 1), note("l", "x") < note("r", "y"))

flush("compare not")

	note("then", nil)
end
flush("branch")

local obj = { n = 0 }
function obj:add(k)
	self.n += k
	return self
end
end
local function getobj()
	note("obj", nil)
	return obj
end
getobj():add(note("arg", 1)):add(note("arg2", 2))
print(obj.n)
flush("method")

local saved = t.v
t.v = "new"
print(saved, t.v)

local len = #box
table.insert(box, 4)
print(len, #box)

	counter += 1
	return counter
end

bump()
print(before, counter)

	i += 1
	return 0
end
